reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Applying the rule to anticoagulated patients or children.
Using the arrival GCS instead of the 2-hour GCS.
name: Canadian CT Head Rule

version.label: Canadian CT Head Rule (Stiell et al. 2001)
version.detail: Five high-risk factors (for neurosurgical intervention) and two medium-risk factors (for brain injury on CT) in adults with minor head injury and GCS 13–15.

purpose: Identifies adults with minor head injury in whom the rule's criteria for CT are met.
intendedPopulation: Adults (16+) with blunt minor head injury, GCS 13–15, and witnessed LOC, definite amnesia or witnessed disorientation.

calculatorNotice.title: Check that the rule applies
calculatorNotice.message: The rule was not derived for children, GCS below 13, anticoagulated patients or obvious open skull fracture. Local protocols may differ (e.g. for anticoagulation).

options.label: Yes: minor head injury in the rule's population
options.detail: Blunt head injury with witnessed loss of consciousness, definite amnesia or witnessed disorientation; GCS 13–15; age 16 or over.

options.label: No: outside the rule
options.detail: e.g. age under 16, GCS under 13, anticoagulation or bleeding disorder, obvious open skull fracture, no loss of consciousness/amnesia/disorientation.

inputDefinitions.label: GCS below 15 at 2 hours after injury
Suspected open or depressed skull fracture
Any sign of basal skull fracture
inputDefinitions.help: Haemotympanum, 'raccoon' eyes, CSF otorrhoea or rhinorrhoea, Battle's sign.

inputDefinitions.label: Amnesia before impact of 30 minutes or more
Dangerous mechanism
inputDefinitions.help: Pedestrian struck by a motor vehicle, occupant ejected from a vehicle, or fall from over 3 feet or 5 stairs.

calculationMethod.display: {total == 0 ? 'Not applicable' : total == 3 ? 'High risk' : total == 2 ? 'Medium risk' : 'No risk factor'}
calculationMethod.share: Canadian CT Head Rule: {total == 0 ? 'rule not applicable' : total == 3 ? 'high-risk factor present' : total == 2 ? 'medium-risk factor present' : 'no risk factors'}

resultStates.label: Rule not applicable
resultStates.summary: The patient is outside the population in which the rule was derived.
resultStates.detail: Use clinical judgement and local protocol.

resultStates.label: High-risk factor present
resultStates.summary: At least one high-risk factor (risk of needing neurosurgical intervention). The rule's criteria for CT are met.
resultStates.detail: Assess according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Medium-risk factor present
resultStates.summary: A medium-risk factor (risk of brain injury on CT) without a high-risk factor. The rule's criteria for CT are met.

resultStates.label: No rule risk factor
resultStates.summary: None of the seven factors is present: the rule's criteria for CT are not met.
resultStates.detail: Clinical judgement and observation still apply; the rule does not exclude injury.

clinicalContext.text: Highly sensitive for injuries needing neurosurgical intervention in its derivation and validation cohorts.
An imaging decision aid, not a substitute for clinical assessment.

clinicalInsights.text: Age 65 or older is a high-risk factor on its own.
Document the GCS at 2 hours after injury, not only on arrival.

limitations.text: Applies only to its derivation population; not to children, anticoagulated patients or GCS below 13.

limitations: Requires reliable history of LOC, amnesia and mechanism.
Local guidelines (e.g. NICE) use different criteria.

confounders.effect: Outside the rule; risk of haemorrhage is higher.

guideSections.what: A decision rule with five high-risk and two medium-risk factors for CT after minor head injury.
guideSections.whenToUse: Adults with minor head injury (GCS 13–15) and LOC, amnesia or disorientation.
guideSections.howToPerform: Confirm the rule applies. Check each high-risk and medium-risk factor. Any factor present meets the rule's criteria for CT.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Supports, but does not replace, clinical judgement and local protocol.

sources.citation: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen K, et al. The Canadian CT Head Rule for patients with minor head injury. Lancet. 2001;357(9266):1391-1396.
